item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01090","case1_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 120/2 by dividing twice to get 30, then asserts 15.","case2_error":"Provides unsupported $5.00 after a correct difference expression, whose value is $4.00.","reason":"Case 1 shows an explicit numerical evaluation error; case 2 supplies an incorrect final number without showing its calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01091","case1_error":"Reverses the described chronology and subtracts both cuts, but the question ambiguously identifies the boards and their lengths.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 10 + 14 + 17 as 31 instead of 41.","reason":"Case 1's contradictory description of board lengths and cutting each board makes the requested quantity materially ambiguous; the reference does not resolve this.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J01092","case1_error":"Omits the $20 flat fee from the total deposit.","case2_error":"Uses all 30 students as the last group's size instead of subtracting the 25 already assigned.","reason":"One omits a fixed additive charge; the other substitutes the whole population for a remaining subgroup in the divisor.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01093","case1_error":"States an unsupported $12,000 after the correct formula, which yields $23,248.","case2_error":"Answers Tully's current age, 61, instead of his age one year ago, 60.","reason":"An unsupported final number after a correct formula differs from correctly calculating and reporting the wrong requested quantity.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01094","case1_error":"Treats Frank's sold third, 12 apples, as his remaining apples instead of subtracting it from 36.","case2_error":"Subtracts stored sections from the original 40, ignoring the 10 sections already given away.","reason":"Case 1 confuses the removed portion with the remainder; case 2 uses the original total instead of the updated remainder.","judgment":"different"}]}
